name: How do I know if my garage foundation is strong enough?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether my existing garage slab and foundation can support a conversion without major reinforcement?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell whether my existing garage slab and foundation can support a conversion without major reinforcement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The foundation is one of the biggest unknowns in any garage conversion because the existing slab may have been built for vehicle storage, not habitable use. Visible cracks do not always mean failure, but they can signal settlement, drainage problems, or structural movement that must be evaluated. If the slab is uneven, damaged by water, or too thin for the planned conversion, the project may require repair or strengthening. An experienced contractor or structural engineer should inspect the garage early, especially if the home is older or the lot has drainage issues. This matters because foundation work can be one of the most expensive surprises in the project. Homeowners often want to know whether a slab is “good enough,” but the answer depends on the intended use, local code, and the condition of the rest of the structure. A conversion should not move forward on assumptions alone. If the foundation is questionable, the safest step is to evaluate it before investing in full design and permit drawings.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage foundation can only be judged reliably after a site inspection, measurements, and sometimes engineering review. Cracks, settlement, moisture, and undersized footings can all mean the slab needs repair or reinforcement before a legal conversion can proceed.
